eyebrow: Rendez-vous — one room, one agent, one artifact, many humans
title: Work is multiplayer. Agents are single-player.
bullets: Every agent you use today lives in exactly one person's window.
So the human becomes the integration layer: copy-paste between two chat windows.
A screenshot forwarded to the other side. “Let me ask the AI and get back to you.”
The second person never sees the context.
The deliverable dies inside one private thread.

title: Four members. Four surfaces. One session.

ladderRows.sends: what only a local machine knows
ladderRows.receives: the same transcript as the humans

caption: No install. No shared login. No new app. The room models members, not humans — which is why a machine joins the same way a person does.

eyebrow: It works — live, on real surfaces
title: Not a mock. A real phone, a real thread, a real artifact.

timelineItems.label: A real phone types “new” on Telegram — the room exists
Cold boot: agent session and shared artifact both ready
A second person joins from a laptop; a desktop agent joins as a member
A voice note is transcribed and attributed to whoever sent it
A photo is described by the agent and written into the artifact
“@me” — one member gets the answer, the others see only that a whisper happened
The agent replies with a voice note, and attaches real files
Killed mid-session, the room comes back still knowing what was discussed

caption: Every row observed end to end on live infrastructure, not described.

title: One pipeline, four layers, one seam that matters.
bullets: agentpush — every channel behind one API, in and out. The room never learns a provider's quirks.
Rendez-vous — the room: members, attribution, fan-out by presence tier, the authority to send.
agentproto — our own open-source agent runtime. Unmodified, straight from npm.
e2b — one sandbox per room, holding the shared artifact. OpenAI for voice and vision, canvakit for the PDF.
code:
Telegram · WhatsApp · Email · Web · a desktop agent
                    │
              [ agentpush ]        ingress + egress, one API
                    │
             [ RENDEZ-VOUS ]       members · attribution · fan-out
                    │
              [ agentproto ]       the agent runtime — swappable
                    │
                 [ e2b ]           one sandbox, one artifact URL
highlight: The runtime sits under a clean seam. That is the whole claim: swap it and the room does not move.
caption: Built against five silent upstream failures we found and fixed on the way — none of which crashed, all of which lost data or reported success while doing nothing.

eyebrow: Work leaves the room — on purpose
title: A room with a notion of authority, not a relay.

findingsItems.label: A member asks the room for the deliverable — a PDF of what everyone just built
the room previews it first: recipient, channel, subject, the rendered document — and sends nothing until a member explicitly confirms
it lands on a phone as a real file, and in an inbox, addressed to someone who was never in the room
the send is written into the shared transcript: who asked, who confirmed, what, to whom

highlight: Every other capability keeps work inside the room. This one lets it leave — under the members' control, on the record.

title: One shape, five independent silent failures.

findingsItems.label: a killed session still answers 200 — resume reported success in 0.7s having resumed nothing
omit queue: true and a message arriving mid-turn is rejected and lost
the fan-out cursor freezes on resume — every reply after it vanishes
an account-pinned inbound route is filtered out and never fires
the agent proposes rebuilding a Gmail capability the workspace already brokered

highlight: Four of these lost data quietly. One reported success while doing nothing. None crash; all look like working code or correct configuration.
caption: Each one is fixed, with a regression test. This is why the room records who asked and who confirmed.

title: What we have not proven.
bullets: Paused sandboxes expire in 20–60 minutes. One did, live, mid-rehearsal — the room advertised a dead link until we made box liveness its own fact.
WhatsApp is not provisioned: no number, no key. The room is channel-agnostic by construction, so it is a config change, not code.
We share an existing workspace's Telegram routing; a catch-all route there could fire alongside ours.
Swapping the runtime for Codex failed at the auth gate, not the swap — a fresh box has no login. The credential model is the real work.
